There's a function "holidays" that takes country code and year. That will return a dictionary mapping dates to holiday names. Then we need to identify which holidays are considered long weekends. Typically, a long weekend occurs when a holiday falls on a Friday or Monday (or sometimes Thursday or Tuesday if there's a bridge). But the user didn't specify definition. They want "long weekends". Usually it's holidays that create a three-day weekend. In Canada, there are federal holidays: New Year's Day, Family Day (varies), Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Remembrance Day, Christmas, Boxing Day. Some provinces have additional holidays.

Then find those that fall on Friday or Monday. Also maybe include holidays that fall on Thursday or Tuesday but only if they are observed on the nearest weekday? Actually many holidays are observed on the nearest weekday if they fall on weekend. For example, if a holiday falls on Saturday, it's observed on Friday; if it falls on Sunday, observed on Monday. So we should consider observed dates too. The "holidays" library returns observed dates as well. So we can just check each holiday's date. If it's a Friday or Monday, then it's a long weekend. But the user might want the official long weekends. Let's assume they want holidays that create at least a three-day weekend.
